sections.h2: What makes the Leland market move quickly?
sections.html:
Growth defines Leland. Census estimates show 35,731 people in July 2025, a 52.9% jump above the 23,365 base for April 2020, and the town had only 13,527 residents at the 2010 count.

Its land area is 19.94 square miles, within Brunswick County. Newer neighborhoods and a renovated Founders Park give buyers a lot to look at, so an older or worn house needs realistic pricing. Owners usually compare a cash sale, an agent listing and a private sale.

Leland skews toward owners and older residents. Census QuickFacts reports owners in 80.6% of homes, 28.4% of the population at 65 or more, and only 16.3% under 18.

sections.h2: Which tax office covers Leland, and what is the revaluation schedule?
sections.html:
Leland parcels are appraised, billed and collected by the Brunswick County Tax Office. Its site announces the next countywide revaluation, valued as of January 1, 2027.

The county timeline gives the sequence. All real property is valued on its market value and condition as of January 1, 2027, and buildings still under construction on that date are valued by percentage complete. Owners should receive notices between February and March 2027 and should compare them with the property record card. The assessor can adjust values in an informal review until the equalization board meets. After that, appeals become formal and are argued before the board. Filing after adjournment is too late for that year, and a changed value reaches forward only.

  • Bills for 2026 went out in mid-August and stay free of interest until January 5, 2027.
  • Visit the David R. Sandifer Administration Building in Bolivia or call 910-253-2829.
  • The Tax Office can name the rates for your parcel.

sections.h2: How do Leland budgets relate to my tax bill?
sections.html:
Leland's Town Council approved a $50 million budget covering fiscal 2026-2027, which starts July 1, 2026 and ends June 30, 2027, and the town says the balanced budget reflects a 7.4% reduction in the tax rate.

A buyer weighing two houses will compare total tax bills, and the Tax Office can name the rates for your address. State law sets the due date at September 1 and ties unpaid amounts to the parcel, so a closing office pays any balance from your proceeds.

sections.h2: Which Leland projects affect a sale?
sections.html:
The town's own website points to several projects. It describes the Leland 2045 Comprehensive Plan, adopted in November 2021, which guides goals across departments, and a Unified Development Ordinance under development to consolidate rules now spread across several documents.

  • Founders Park at 113 Town Hall Drive reopened after renovation, with an amphitheater, splash pad and event programming.
  • The Leland Cultural Arts Center at 1212 Magnolia Village Way hosts community events, including a yearly Hurricane Expo for residents.
  • The Town Council has passed resolutions about the Cape Fear Memorial Bridge replacement project, including a request for an environmental impact statement.
  • A Wilmington-area planning grant of $973,600 supports a multi-use path along S. Navassa Rd.
  • The town resurfaces roughly 5% of its roads each year to match a typical 20-year lifespan.

The town also revised its rules for poultry, livestock and wild animals, with citations issued by its police department. Owners who keep animals on the lot should read the rules before listing.

sections.h2: What town services should Leland sellers know about?
sections.html:
Town Hall sits at 102 Town Hall Drive, next to Founders Park at 113 Town Hall Drive, and the town runs its own police and fire departments. The town's site notes that the Leland Police Department earned accreditation from the North Carolina Law Enforcement Accreditation program, and the town has launched a transparency portal and a mobile app called Leland Connect for residents.

  • The town has imposed burn bans because of unfavorable weather, such as one issued June 9 and lifted September 15 in 2026, so check before burning yard debris.
  • Brunswick County Board of Elections in Bolivia, not the town, manages elections.
  • The Leland Citizens Academy offers a six-week look at local government for residents.

Buyers moving from out of the area often ask how storms are handled, and the annual Hurricane Expo at the Cultural Arts Center is one example of the town's outreach. Mention these community features in your listing or conversation with a buyer, because they speak to daily life in Leland.

sections.h2: What relief exists for retirees, veterans and heirs in Leland?
sections.html:
Because Leland has many older residents and 2,946 veterans, state relief programs matter here. A disabled veteran who qualifies sees $45,000 of appraised value on the permanent residence excluded, and NCDOR's own form says no age or income limit applies. An unmarried surviving spouse may also qualify, and the county assessor takes the application.

The NCDOR form asks for filing in the listing period and takes late filings up to June 1, and circuit breaker applicants refile annually. An owner can draw on just one of the three programs, so the assessor can tell you which fits.

A separate circuit breaker holds tax to 4.0% of income for qualifying owners aged 65 or more, or permanently disabled, whose income is at or under the limit, and to 5.0% when income runs above the limit but within 150% of it. NCDOR lists $38,800 and $58,200 for 2026. The home must have been owned and occupied for five years. The deferred difference is a lien, and the most recent three years of it come due on a sale or transfer.

After a death, the clerk of court in the decedent's home county can accept a small-estate affidavit for personal property up to $20,000. A house usually calls for more steps, so ask the clerk or an attorney how to clear title before listing.

sections.h2: Which sale method fits a Leland house?
sections.html:
Weigh speed, price and effort. A traditional listing can reward a well-kept house, though you handle showings, repair talks and a buyer's loan timeline. A direct cash sale moves faster and buys the house despite its flaws, which may mean a lower price.

  • An agent fits an updated house and a patient owner.
  • A private sale fits an owner who knows the market.
  • A cash sale helps when damage, deferred repairs, tenants or an estate house would slow a listing.

Keep every offer in writing, learn who covers closing costs and have your attorney check the figures.

faqs.q: When is Brunswick County's next revaluation?
faqs.a: January 1, 2027 is the effective date, and the county timeline schedules owner notices for February and March 2027.

faqs.q: What is the process to dispute a Brunswick County value?
faqs.a: Request an informal review from the Tax Office, or present a formal appeal after the county's equalization board convenes. Filing after adjournment generally waits for the next year.

faqs.q: When are Leland property taxes due?
faqs.a: September 1 each year. For 2026 the county says bills are interest-free through January 5, 2027, and that a weekend deadline slides to the next business day.

faqs.q: What does the average Leland house sell for?
faqs.a: Census QuickFacts gives a $398,900 midpoint value for owned homes over 2020 to 2024. A particular house varies with age, size, location and condition.

faqs.q: Can a disabled veteran lower a Leland tax bill?
faqs.a: Possibly. For a qualifying disabled veteran, $45,000 of the residence's appraised value is excluded, and NCDOR's form lists no age or income cap. A Veterans Service Officer completes the first part, and the county assessor takes the form.
